aspects.says: computeIfAbsent records nothing when its function returns null, so a memo built on it calls the function again for every such key.
basis: section:A Memoized Function Must Be Pure, and Its Computation Must Not Go Back Into the Map

aspects.says: Function.identity() returns one shared object, different from UnaryOperator.identity(), and either it or x -> x works as a toMap mapper.
aspects.reason: which object a factory returns is not behaviour a solution should depend on, so there is nothing for a test to grade; the type point it leads to is graded by the quiz's first question

aspects.says: A memo whose function asks the same ConcurrentHashMap for other keys inside computeIfAbsent can fail with IllegalStateException: Recursive update; computing outside the map and storing with putIfAbsent works.
basis: section:A Memoized Function Must Be Pure, and Its Computation Must Not Go Back Into the Map

aspects.says: A merge function that keeps the value seen last is wrong when input arrives out of order; BinaryOperator.maxBy with a Comparator keeps the one the data says is newest.
basis: section:A Merge Function Picks a Winner, and the Last One Seen Isn't Always the Newest

aspects.says: Map.merge stores the given value for an absent key without calling the function.
basis: section:A Remapping Function That Returns null Removes the Entry

aspects.says: The javadoc of minBy and maxBy doesn't say which operand wins a tie; on Java 21 it is the first, and a tie-breaker in the comparator removes the question.
basis: section:A Merge Function Picks a Winner, and the Last One Seen Isn't Always the Newest
aspects.reason: the tie behaviour is an undocumented implementation detail, which a graded test must not pin; the page tells the reader not to rely on it

aspects.says: andThen passes a null result on to the next step, which throws; Optional.map stops at the first null, so the steps after it don't run.
basis: section:A null Halfway Through an andThen Chain Fails in the Next Step; Optional.map Stops There

aspects.says: UnaryOperator<T> extends Function<T, T>, so a Function<T, T> variable can't be passed where a UnaryOperator<T> is asked for; a lambda written in the call can, and a cast compiles but throws ClassCastException.
basis: section:UnaryOperator<T> Is a Function<T, T>, but a Function<T, T> Is Not a UnaryOperator<T>

aspects.says: ConcurrentHashMap throws on a recursive update only when it detects one, so a small test can pass where a larger input fails.
basis: section:A Memoized Function Must Be Pure, and Its Computation Must Not Go Back Into the Map

aspects.says: An entry removed by a null from a remapping function is gone for every later operation, including bulk ones like replaceAll that only touch existing entries.
basis: section:A Remapping Function That Returns null Removes the Entry

aspects.says: A remapping function given to compute, computeIfPresent or merge removes the entry when it returns null; returning the old value leaves the entry as it is.
basis: section:A Remapping Function That Returns null Removes the Entry

aspects.says: Collectors.toMap throws IllegalStateException on a duplicate key unless given a merge function, and NullPointerException on a null value even with one, so nulls are handled before the collector.
basis: section:Collectors.toMap Throws on a Duplicate Key or a null Value Until You Say What to Do

aspects.says: A merge function doesn't make toMap accept null values: the three-argument form collects through Map.merge, which rejects null.
basis: section:Collectors.toMap Throws on a Duplicate Key or a null Value Until You Say What to Do
